question: I’m 63, receiving CPP retirement benefits and working at a CPP-covered job. Can I opt out of CPP contributions now?
generated_answer:
In Canada, if you're 65 or older and receiving Canada Pension Plan (CPP) retirement benefits, you can choose to stop contributing to the CPP. However, if you're under 65, you must continue to contribute to the CPP if you're working and earning a salary from a CPP-covered job.

Since you're 63 and still working, you're required to continue making CPP contributions, even though you're already receiving CPP retirement benefits. You won't be able to opt out of CPP contributions until you turn 65.

It's worth noting that continuing to contribute to the CPP while receiving benefits can potentially increase your retirement benefits. The additional contributions you make will be used to calculate your Post-Retirement Benefit (PRB), which can result in a higher monthly benefit amount.

Once you turn 65, you can choose to stop contributing to the CPP by completing Form CPT30, Election to Stop Contributing to the Canada Pension Plan. You can submit this form to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or to your employer.

Keep in mind that if you stop contributing to the CPP, you won't be eligible to earn additional PRB credits, which could impact your future benefit amounts.

It's always a good idea to consult with a financial advisor or a Service Canada representative to discuss your specific situation and determine the best course of action for your individual circumstances.
